transcript.text: In most Massachusetts races there's no competition, one candidate, one party, no choice. Why does that matter? Think about the only coffee shop in town. If nobody else can open across the street, the prices go up and the service goes down. Nobody has to try. Politics works the same way. When politicians don't have to compete, they don't have to listen. Question 3 opens the door. All candidates, one primary, and the best two move on. That's how you get representatives who actually listen.
